newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open stagnant, baht fears linger.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open stagnant, baht fears linger.

text.p: Singapore shares opened stagnant on Thursday with most stocks narrowly stuck around the previous day's levels while others succumbed to lingering baht woes.
Dealers said the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was dampened early by the drop in food company Cerebos Pacific, which slipped to new lows on its exposure to Thailand.
The stock fell to a low of Singapore $5.70, and was later at S$5.85, down 25 cents.
At 0220 GMT, the STII was down 4.10 points at 1,964.81.
"The market is stagnant. It's around overnight prices and at very small volumes," a dealer with a Singapore brokerage said.

Institutional demand was confined to core stocks like banks. Malaysian over-the-counter stocks, which gained on a spillover feverish run-up in Thailand on Wednesday, drew less interest as attention turned to Hong Kong's bullish Hang Seng.
Thailand on Wednesday allowed the baht to be floated with its value no longer set by a basket of currencies.
Raffles Medical Group hit new highs at S$1.09 in active dealing due to speculative trading spurred along by rumours of a possible takeover, dealers said.
Lung Kee Metal also hit a high of US$1.24, to trade later around US$1.22.
Some dealers said U.S.-dollar denominated issues were aided by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged after its policy meeting on Wednesday.
